perf.summary: Fuse the three-array init loop and combine the leaves/isolated scan with degree computation.
perf.currentCost: Init loop writes tin,low,comp in one pass (already fused) but comp degree pass plus a separate scan over compCount to count leaves/isolated is two passes over component data. Also degree[] is zeroed in its own loop.
perf.proposedChange: Zero degree[] inside the same allocation-adjacent loop, and after ComputeComponentDegrees the leaves/isolated counting loop is unavoidable, but `leaves / 2` and `(leaves + 1) / 2` divides by 2 on a provably non-negative int can be `leaves >> 1` and `(leaves + 1) >> 1`.
perf.rationale: Signed `/2` emits an extra add-of-sign-bit sequence (test sign, conditionally add 1, then shift) because the compiler must round toward zero for negatives. leaves and isolated are counts (>=0), so `>>1` is one instruction and identical for non-negative operands.
perf.risk: Strength reduction `x/2 -> x>>1` only matches for x>=0; leaves is a count incremented from 0 so always >=0, and leaves+1>=1>=0. Safe. Burst/Roslyn may already do this; if leaves were ever negative the results would differ, but it cannot be.

perf.summary: Hoist comp[u] out of the inner edge loop.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop reads comp[u] on every edge via `comp[u] != comp[to[e]]` and `degree[comp[u]]++`, dereferencing comp[u] up to 3 times per edge though u is loop-invariant in the inner loop.
perf.proposedChange: In the outer loop body load `int cu = comp[u]; int hu = head[u];` once, then inner loop: `if (cu != comp[to[e]]) degree[cu]++;`.
perf.rationale: comp[u] is invariant across the entire inner edge traversal; hoisting removes a load and an address computation per edge, and `degree[cu]` indexes off a register instead of re-loading comp[u]. Fewer cache touches of comp[] in the hot adjacency walk.
perf.risk: None: comp[u] and head[u] are not modified inside the inner loop. Pure hoist.
